why: tables#68 — ONE corpus, two runners. The natural order of a table label is computed in two places by necessity: the paginated Tables list is ordered by the SERVER (queries/tables_list.sql -> number_sort), because a browser sorting the visible page would order each page on its own and still cut the pages by the wrong key; the POS picker and the floor plan re-group rows in the browser. Two implementations of one rule drift, and they did: the SQL only padded the FINAL run of digits, so 'Barra 2 Bis' and 'Barra 10 Bis' came out in opposite orders on the two screens. This file is the rule. tests/floor.postgres.test.py reads it and asserts against real Postgres; ui/lib/natural-order.test.ts reads it and asserts against the comparator. Whichever side drifts turns red.
rule: Every run of digits is compared as a NUMBER, wherever it sits in the label (start, middle or end); everything else is compared as text in the active locale. Implemented as: left-pad every digit run to 12 characters, then compare the padded labels.
